title: Harden Cancel against blocked network and cloud calls (CancelSynchronousIo plus ERROR_OPERATION_ABORTED 995 as cancellation)
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

Existing tests cover the aborted or blocked-call path: missing

Spike 3 (a stalled, established SMB session: cancel returns 995, and the CloseHandle and dispose afterwards return within 2 s) did not run because Defender blocks impacket. A person with admin must either add a Defender exclusion for the spike's scratch venv or supply a different unelevated SMB2 server on port 4450. Without that, close-after-abort latency is unmeasured and this slice ships on the reading that it is fast. Do you want it measured, or is the residual risk accepted?

The share test FAILS as VOID when the network fails fast, so an offline laptop gets a red suite. The alternative is a skip or a filterable trait, which keeps the suite green but lets a green run hide that no blocked call was exercised. The design chose the loud failure. The project's 'never skipped' rule is stated for counting-rule tests, not this one.
A fixed 25 ms retry forever, against a backoff. The spike measured one cancel never returning, and the loop only runs while a cancelled call is still in flight, so fixed was kept.
A new dedicated thread per cancel, against a ThreadPool task. A thread is used because the loop sleeps and the pool may be starved, but a Task.Run would also work.
Whether an interrupted folder deserves its own visible flag (a store bit and a UI panel) instead of sharing the state of never-reached folders. Deferred to a slice that owns the screen.

A scan that completed without a Cancel still waits for the volume query. On a mapped drive whose server stopped answering, that can be as long as the SMB client waits. Cancel stays enabled during that wait and ends it. Whether to also skip the query for DriveType.Network roots is a product choice; the reviewer offered it as optional.

The stalled-session limit from build 3 still stands: a Cancel on a share that stops answering mid-listing waits 62 to 66 s for the SMB client. Only abandoning the scan thread, the design's rejected fallback, would shorten it. That is a decision for design-slice or a person.

Scratch folders %TEMP%\taad-sl024-o031, %TEMP%\taad-sl024-smb and %TEMP%\taad-sl024-respike, and the gitignored artifacts/publish, are left in place. Their evidence is copied into the slice, so they can be deleted.
